I'm 58 this year, and I've been farming these 10 mu for 35 years since my father handed them over. I only finished primary school, so I don't bother much with those books the extension office puts out. I watch what my neighbors do, especially Old Wang who farms just east of me — if he changes something and it works, I pay attention.

I've got 10.1 mu split into two pieces. 6.1 mu I do wheat-maize double crop, that's my main field. The other 4 mu I plant cotton — my wife handles the cotton because we get cash in the fall when the maize price is still uncertain. My son works at a factory in Handan, so it's just me and my wife most days. He comes back for wheat harvest and maize planting, which is good because that week between crops you barely have time to breathe. Last year I tried to do it alone and nearly didn't get the maize in on time.

For the wheat, I planted it last October with seed I saved from the year before. I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu then — that's not quite a full bag for each mu, but it's what I can afford. Now it's April, and I'm looking at the wheat. It looks okay, not great. I'll topdress about 18 kg of urea per mu when it starts jointing — Old Wang did less last year and his wheat was thin, so I'm not cutting back there. I'll irrigate twice: once now at green-up, and again at jointing. Water from the well costs me about 40 yuan each time per mu, so I won't do a third unless it gets really dry. I'd rather waste a bit of fertilizer money than risk a bad yield. I hope for about 400 kg per mu, same as most years. Maybe 450 if the weather cooperates, but I don't count on it.

Cotton goes in now on the four-mu plot. I use local seed, saved from last year too — those hybrid seeds cost too much. I put down about 35 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at sowing. I'll side-dress some urea, maybe 12 kg per mu, when it flowers if it looks hungry. One irrigation at flowering should be enough if we get some rain in July. Cotton needs a lot of picking labor, so my wife and I will be out there every morning in September. We don't hire pickers — that's 100 yuan a day we don't have. I expect about 240 kg of lint per mu if the bollworms don't get bad. I'll spray insecticide twice and herbicide once.

Maize gets planted right after wheat harvest in mid-June, usually by hand because I don't own a planter. Sometimes I hire a small tractor to plow if there's time, but often I just chop the wheat stubble and hoe it in because the window is so tight — you only get a few days. I put down about 35 kg per mu of compound fertilizer at planting, and if the season looks wet and good, I'll topdress another 15 kg of urea at the big trumpet stage. One irrigation at flowering. Maize usually gives me about 420 kg per mu.

Money is always tight. My son sends some money home, but fertilizer prices went up again this spring. I can't afford what the rich farmers on TV do. I use about 14 kg of nitrogen per mu on wheat, a bit less on maize and cotton. It's not what the extension people recommend, but it's what I can pay for without borrowing. I'd rather spend a little more on fertilizer than risk a bad yield — a bad year means debt, and I hate debt. The well water is metered, so I watch every irrigation. But you can't skip fertilizer entirely or you'll have nothing to sell.
